summary: The root ملق (malaqa) primarily means to behave in a loving, affectionate, or blandishing manner towards someone. It implies coaxing or showing excessive fondness.
lane: 5 تَمَلَّقَهُ ذ , (S, K,) and تَمَلَّقَ لَهُ , (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. تَمَلُّقٌ and تِمِلَّاقٌ , [like تِحِمَّالٌ and تِكِلَّامٌ , not تَمْلَاقٌ as in the CK,] He behaved in a loving, or an affectionate, and a blandishing, or coaxing, manner to him. (S, Msb, * K.) See a verse cited in art. رضو , conj. 5.

headwords.def: He flayed him with a whip: like سَلَقَهُ. (TA in art. سلق.)

(S, K,) and تَمَلَّقَ لَهُ, (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. تَمَلُّقٌ and تِمِلَّاقٌ, [like تِحِمَّالٌ and تِكِلَّامٌ, not تَمْلَاقٌ as in the CK,] He behaved in a loving, or an affectionate, and a blandishing, or coaxing, manner to him. (S, Msb, * K.) See a verse cited in art. رضو, conj. 5.
[A swiftly-running mare ]. See عَبَّرَ بِهِ. مَلَّاقٌ Vehement in journeying, or in his pace; i. q. مَلَّاخٌ. (TA, voce مَلَّاخٌ.)

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
